ana_cs: Heads up - Post-onboard feedback from Meridian (Enterprise, CSM=Ravi). They listed three asks blocking broader rollout: route-level spend caps, quickstart embedding prompt patterns for short contexts (<=128 tokens), and clearer per-route quota alerts/export for finance. They said treasury is nervous; could affect renewal if not addressed.

vik_pm: Please drop concrete examples + severity. Is there a workaround?

ana_cs: Examples: - Treasury saw a surprise $12k spike from one route during a batch job. - Developers want sample prompt/embedding configs for product search. - Finance wants downloadable per-route CSV for monthly reconciliation. Workarounds are manual throttling client-side and ad-hoc reports.

ana_cs: Frequency: similar asks from two other customers this sprint (Nova, Beacon).

tess_support: I pulled support threads and screenshots: https://support.example.com/MD-778. Uploaded a 45s screencap showing confusion around the Console quota card.

dave_research: Prioritization heuristics: impact_score = ARR_exposed * mentions. Route spend caps = high impact, medium dev. Templates = low revenue but high time-saved for customers. Quota export = medium impact, low dev.

kia_pdm: Can we get 1-line ask descriptions so I can create PRD stubs? Any compliance or billing constraints?

ana_cs: route spend caps: "Admins can set soft/hard token/spend caps per API route, with alerting and override flows."
templates: "Ship 5 short-context embedding templates + example dataset + README for quick testing."
quota export: "Add per-route monthly token/spend CSV export and dashboard countdown + alert when usage > 80%."

vik_pm: Kia/Dave - quick T-shirt sizes by EOD? Tess - attach the video & logs to tickets. I'll create separate tickets per ask.

slackbot: Created ticket RED-PL-820 (route-caps), RED-PL-821 (embed-templates), RED-PL-822 (quota-export). Linked MD-778.

tess_support: Attached logs and 45s clip to RED-PL-820 and RED-PL-822.

kia_pdm: T-shirt sizes: route caps = L (3w), templates = S (4d), quota export = M (1w). No legal flags surfaced.
